none | footnote = }} ==Culture== ===Society and architecture=== Shikoku has historically been quite isolated and therefore it has kept the original characteristics of Japan for a longer period, especially in regards to vegetation and some architectural techniques. There are many Buddhist temples. The "lost" Shikoku has been described by an American writer, {{ill|Alex Kerr (Japanologist)|en|Alex Kerr (Japanologist)|WD=Q4717298|lt=Alex Kerr|1=Alex Kerr (Japanologist)}}, who lived in a remote mountain village near Oboke (大歩危) for many years from 1970 onwards. {{ill|Ashizuri-Uwakai National Park|en|Ashizuri-Uwakai National Park|WD=Q1132029|lt=Ashizuri-Uwakai National Park|1=Ashizuri-Uwakai National Park}} is located in the south-west part of Shikoku. ===Traditions=== [[File:Yosakoi Performers at Kochi Yosakoi Matsuri 2008 40.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Yosakoi|en|Yosakoi|WD=Q3276119|lt=Yosakoi|1=Yosakoi}} festival]] Shikoku is also famous for its {{ill|Shikoku Pilgrimage|en|Shikoku Pilgrimage|WD=Q1972399|lt=88-temple pilgrimage|1=Shikoku Pilgrimage}} of temples. The pilgrimage was established by the Heian-period Buddhist priest {{ill|Kūkai|en|Kūkai|WD=Q222227|lt=Kūkai|1=Kūkai}}, a native of present-day Zentsūji-cho in Kagawa prefecture. According to legend, Kūkai still appears to pilgrims today. Most modern-day pilgrims travel by bus, rarely choosing the old-fashioned method of going by foot. They are seen wearing white jackets emblazoned with the characters reading ''dōgyō ninin'' ({{lang|ja|同行二人}}) meaning "two traveling together". Tokushima Prefecture also has its annual {{ill|Awa Dance Festival|en|Awa Dance Festival|WD=Q1185363|lt=Awa Dance Festival|1=Awa Dance Festival}} running in August at the time of the {{ill|Obon|en|Obon|WD=Q1154888|lt=Obon|1=Obon}} festival, which attracts thousands of tourists each year from all over Japan and from abroad. Kōchi Prefecture is home to the first annual {{ill|Yosakoi|en|Yosakoi|WD=Q3276119|lt=Yosakoi|1=Yosakoi}} festival. The largest festival in Kōchi, it takes place in August every year and attracts dancers and tourists from all over Japan. ===Food=== [[File:Kama-age sanuki udon by sekido in Takamatsu, Kagawa.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Sanuki udon|en|Sanuki udon|WD=Q1185324|lt=Sanuki udon|1=Sanuki udon}}]] One of the major foods of Shikoku is {{ill|Udon|en|Udon|WD=Q471861|lt=Udon|1=Udon}}.{{Cite web|url = http://www.tourismshikoku.org/learnmore/tastes_shikoku/katsuo-no-tataki|title = tourism shikoku|access-date = 2014-11-27|website = tourism shikoku|publisher = Organization for Promotion of Tourism in Shikoku|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141205115003/http://www.tourismshikoku.org/learnmore/tastes_shikoku/katsuo-no-tataki|archive-date = 2014-12-05}} {{ill|Udon|en|Udon|WD=Q471861|lt=Udon|1=Udon}} is often served hot as a noodle soup in its simplest form, as ''kake udon'', in a mildly flavoured broth called ''[[kakejiru]],'' which is made of {{ill|Dashi|en|Dashi|WD=Q851746|lt=Dashi|1=Dashi}}, soy sauce ([[:en:shōyu|shōyu]]), and {{ill|Mirin|en|Mirin|WD=Q1045910|lt=Mirin|1=Mirin}}. It is usually topped with thinly chopped scallions. Other common toppings include {{ill|Tempura|en|Tempura|WD=Q328709|lt=Tempura|1=Tempura}}, often prawn or ''{{ill|kakiage|en|kakiage|WD=Q3192044|lt=kakiage|1=Kakiage}}'' (a type of mixed tempura {{ill|fritter|en|fritter|WD=Q690292|lt=fritter|1=Fritter}}), or ''[[:en:Aburaage|Aburaage]]'', a type of deep-fried {{ill|Tofu|en|Tofu|WD=Q177378|lt=Tofu|1=Tofu}} pockets seasoned with sugar, mirin, and soy sauce. A thin slice of {{ill|Kamaboko|en|Kamaboko|WD=Q166204|lt=Kamaboko|1=Kamaboko}}, a halfmoon-shaped fish cake, is often added. {{ill|Shichimi|en|Shichimi|WD=Q1148919|lt=Shichimi|1=Shichimi}} can be added to taste. Another specialty is {{ill|Kōchi, Kōchi|en|Kōchi, Kōchi|WD=Q200251|lt=Kōchi|1=Kōchi, Kōchi}}'s signature dish, seared {{ill|Bonito|en|Bonito|WD=Q3473576|lt=Bonito|1=Bonito}}. The warm climate of Shikoku lends itself to the cultivation of citrus fruits. As a result, {{ill|Yuzu|en|Yuzu|WD=Q867776|lt=Yuzu|1=Yuzu}}, [[:en:Mikan|Mikan]] and other citrus fruits are plentiful on Shikoku and have become synonymous with the regions they are grown in. ===Movements=== Pioneering {{ill|natural farming|en|natural farming|WD=Q2281159|lt=natural farmer|1=Natural farming}} {{ill|Masanobu Fukuoka|en|Masanobu Fukuoka|WD=Q334997|lt=Masanobu Fukuoka|1=Masanobu Fukuoka}}, author of ''{{ill|The One-Straw Revolution|en|The One-Straw Revolution|WD=Q3823944|lt=The One-Straw Revolution|1=The One-Straw Revolution}}'', developed his methods here on his family's farm. ===Sports=== [[File:Botchan Stadium(20160416) 02.jpg|thumb|left|{{ill|Shikoku Island League Plus|en|Shikoku Island League Plus|WD=Q5366286|lt=Shikoku Island League Plus|1=Shikoku Island League Plus}} ({{ill|Ehime Mandarin Pirates|en|Ehime Mandarin Pirates|WD=Q2109810|lt=Ehime Mandarin Pirates|1=Ehime Mandarin Pirates}})]] [[File:Naruto Athletic 1.JPG|thumb|[[:en:J. League|J. League]] ({{ill|Tokushima Vortis|en|Tokushima Vortis|WD=Q513145|lt=Tokushima Vortis|1=Tokushima Vortis}})]] Historically no Shikoku-based [[:en:sports|sports]] team has competed in the top Japanese division of [[:en:Japanese baseball|baseball]], {{ill|Football in Japan|en|Football in Japan|WD=Q1417709|lt=football (soccer)|1=Football in Japan}} or even {{ill|Rugby union in Japan|en|Rugby union in Japan|WD=Q3452890|lt=rugby union|1=Rugby union in Japan}}. However, Tokushima Vortis have had two spells in the top flight of Japanese soccer ({{ill|J1 League|en|J1 League|WD=Q276445|lt=J1|1=J1 League}}) in 2014 and 2021. Currently the major teams competing in Shikoku's major cities include: *{{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|WD=Q460812|lt=Naruto|1=Naruto, Tokushima}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}: {{ill|Tokushima Vortis|en|Tokushima Vortis|WD=Q513145|lt=Tokushima Vortis|1=Tokushima Vortis}} (football, {{ill|J2 League|en|J2 League|WD=Q1140581|lt=J2|1=J2 League}}); {{ill|Tokushima Indigo Socks|en|Tokushima Indigo Socks|WD=Q7813767|lt=Tokushima Indigo Socks|1=Tokushima Indigo Socks}} (baseball, [[:en:Shikoku-Kyūshū Island League|SKIL]]) *{{ill|Matsuyama|en|Matsuyama|WD=Q200022|lt=Matsuyama|1=Matsuyama}}, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|WD=Q123376|lt=Ehime|1=Ehime Prefecture}}: {{ill|Ehime FC|en|Ehime FC|WD=Q1059329|lt=Ehime FC|1=Ehime FC}} (football, J2); {{ill|Ehime Mandarin Pirates|en|Ehime Mandarin Pirates|WD=Q2109810|lt=Ehime Mandarin Pirates|1=Ehime Mandarin Pirates}} (baseball, SKIL) *{{ill|Imabari, Ehime|en|Imabari, Ehime|WD=Q461020|lt=Imabari|1=Imabari, Ehime}}, {{ill|Ehime Prefecture|en|Ehime Prefecture|WD=Q123376|lt=Ehime|1=Ehime Prefecture}}: {{ill|FC Imabari|en|FC Imabari|WD=Q11198999|lt=FC Imabari|1=FC Imabari}} (football, {{ill|J3 League|en|J3 League|WD=Q6106324|lt=J3|1=J3 League}}); *{{ill|Takamatsu|en|Takamatsu|WD=Q200707|lt=Takamatsu|1=Takamatsu}}, {{ill|Kagawa Prefecture|en|Kagawa Prefecture|WD=Q161454|lt=Kagawa|1=Kagawa Prefecture}}: {{ill|Kamatamare Sanuki|en|Kamatamare Sanuki|WD=Q4210742|lt=Kamatamare Sanuki|1=Kamatamare Sanuki}} (football, J3); {{ill|Kagawa Olive Guyners|en|Kagawa Olive Guyners|WD=Q6346401|lt=Kagawa Olive Guyners|1=Kagawa Olive Guyners}} (baseball, SKIL) *{{ill|Kōchi, Kōchi|en|Kōchi, Kōchi|WD=Q200251|lt=Kōchi|1=Kōchi, Kōchi}}, {{ill|Kōchi Prefecture|en|Kōchi Prefecture|WD=Q134093|lt=Kōchi|1=Kōchi Prefecture}}: [[:en:Kōchi United SC|Kōchi United SC]] (football, {{ill|Japan Football League|en|Japan Football League|WD=Q1370603|lt=JFL|1=Japan Football League}}); {{ill|Kōchi Fighting Dogs|en|Kōchi Fighting Dogs|WD=Q6455084|lt=Kōchi Fighting Dogs|1=Kōchi Fighting Dogs}} (baseball, SKIL) ===Notable sportspeople=== Two time darts Women's World Champion {{ill|Mikuru Suzuki|en|Mikuru Suzuki|WD=Q59660294|lt=Mikuru Suzuki|1=Mikuru Suzuki}} is a native of Takamatsu in Kagawa Prefecture on Shikoku.{{cite web |title=Japan's Miracle Takes Darts World by Storm |url=https://www.france24.com/en/20190410-japans-miracle-suzuki-takes-darts-world-storm |website=France24.com |date=10 April 2019 |publisher=France 24 |access-date=7 August 2020}} == Transportation == [[File:Kochi_Castle09.JPG|thumb|{{ill|Kōchi Castle|en|Kōchi Castle|WD=Q1012815|lt=Kōchi Castle|1=Kōchi Castle}}]] [[File:Onsenzan-anrakuji-tahouto.JPG|thumb|Anraku-ji in Kamiita, [[:en:Tokushima, Tokushima|Tokushima]]]] ===Roads=== Shikoku is connected to Honshu by three {{ill|Expressways of Japan|en|Expressways of Japan|WD=Q1133841|lt=expressways|1=Expressways of Japan}}, which together form the {{ill|Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project|en|Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project|WD=Q4176108|lt=Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project|1=Honshū–Shikoku Bridge Project}}. * [[Honshū-Shikoku Bridge Project#Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway]] (Eastern Shikoku) * {{ill|Nishiseto Expressway|en|Nishiseto Expressway|WD=Q1799184|lt=Nishiseto Expressway|1=Nishiseto Expressway}} (Western Shikoku) * [[Honshū-Shikoku Bridge Project#Seto-Chūō Expressway|Seto-Chūō Expressway]] (Central Shikoku) The eastern gateway to Shikoku, {{ill|Naruto, Tokushima|en|Naruto, Tokushima|WD=Q460812|lt=Naruto|1=Naruto, Tokushima}} in {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}} has been linked to the [[Honshū-Shikoku Bridge Project#Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway|Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway]] since 1998. This line connects Shikoku to the {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region|1=Kansai region}} area which has a large population, including the large {{ill|conurbation|en|conurbation|WD=Q245260|lt=conurbation|1=Conurbation}}s of {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka|1=Osaka}}, {{ill|Kyoto|en|Kyoto|WD=Q34600|lt=Kyoto|1=Kyoto}}, and {{ill|Kobe|en|Kobe|WD=Q48320|lt=Kobe|1=Kobe}}. Therefore, the Kobe-Awaji-Naruto Expressway carries a large traffic volume. Many highway buses are operated between {{ill|Kansai region|en|Kansai region|WD=Q164256|lt=Kansai region|1=Kansai region}} and {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|WD=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture|1=Tokushima Prefecture}}. The central part of Shikoku is connected to Honshu by ferry, air, and – since 1988 – by the {{ill|Great Seto Bridge|en|Great Seto Bridge|WD=Q976648|lt=Great Seto Bridge|1=Great Seto Bridge}} network. Until completion of the bridges, the region was isolated from the rest of Japan. The freer movement between Honshu and Shikoku was expected to promote economic development on both sides of the bridges, which has not materialized yet. Within the island, a web of {{ill|national highways of Japan|en|national highways of Japan|WD=Q926383|lt=national highways|1=National highways of Japan}} connects the major population centers. These include {{ill|Japan National Route 11|en|Japan National Route 11|WD=Q1138640|lt=Routes 11|1=Japan National Route 11}}, {{ill|Japan National Route 32|en|Japan National Route 32|WD=Q6157226|lt=32|1=Japan National Route 32}}, {{ill|Japan National Route 33|en|Japan National Route 33|WD=Q6157264|lt=33|1=Japan National Route 33}}, {{ill|Japan National Route 55|en|Japan National Route 55|WD=Q6157738|lt=55|1=Japan National Route 55}}, and {{ill|Japan National Route 56|en|Japan National Route 56|WD=Q5644810|lt=56|1=Japan National Route 56}}. ===Rail=== The {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|en|Shikoku Railway Company|WD=Q496531|lt=Shikoku Railway Company|1=Shikoku Railway Company}} (JR Shikoku) serves the island and connects to Honshu via the {{ill|Great Seto Bridge|en|Great Seto Bridge|WD=Q976648|lt=Great Seto Bridge|1=Great Seto Bridge}}. JR lines include: * {{ill|Dosan Line|en|Dosan Line|WD=Q861077|lt=Dosan Line|1=Dosan Line}} * [[:en:Honshi Bisan Line|Honshi Bisan Line]] * {{ill|Kōtoku Line|en|Kōtoku Line|WD=Q859984|lt=Kōtoku Line|1=Kōtoku Line}} * {{ill|Mugi Line|en|Mugi Line|WD=Q860478|lt=Mugi Line|1=Mugi Line}} * {{ill|Naruto Line|en|Naruto Line|WD=Q861091|lt=Naruto Line|1=Naruto Line}} * [[:en:Seto Ōhashi Line|Seto Ōhashi Line]] * {{ill|Tokushima Line|en|Tokushima Line|WD=Q899310|lt=Tokushima Line|1=Tokushima Line}} * {{ill|Uchiko Line|en|Uchiko Line|WD=Q899464|lt=Uchiko Line|1=Uchiko Line}} * {{ill|Yodo Line|en|Yodo Line|WD=Q899418|lt=Yodo Line|1=Yodo Line}} * {{ill|Yosan Line|en|Yosan Line|WD=Q575016|lt=Yosan Line|1=Yosan Line}} Private railway lines operate in each of the four prefectures on Shikoku. === Air travel === Shikoku lacks a full international airport but has four regional/domestic airports ({{ill|Tokushima Airport|en|Tokushima Airport|WD=Q1142453|lt=Tokushima Airport|1=Tokushima Airport}}, {{ill|Takamatsu Airport|en|Takamatsu Airport|WD=Q1334603|lt=Takamatsu Airport|1=Takamatsu Airport}}, [[:en:Ryoma Airport|Kōchi Ryōma Airport]] and {{ill|Matsuyama Airport|en|Matsuyama Airport|WD=Q255345|lt=Matsuyama Airport|1=Matsuyama Airport}}). All of these airports have flights to Tokyo and other major Japanese cities such as {{ill|Osaka|en|Osaka|WD=Q35765|lt=Osaka|1=Osaka}}, {{ill|Nagoya|en|Nagoya|WD=Q11751|lt=Nagoya|1=Nagoya}}, {{ill|Sapporo|en|Sapporo|WD=Q37951|lt=Sapporo|1=Sapporo}}, and [[:en:Fukuoka, Fukuoka|Fukuoka]]. International flights to {{ill|Seoul|en|Seoul|WD=Q8684|lt=Seoul|1=Seoul}}, {{ill|South Korea|en|South Korea|WD=Q884|lt=South Korea|1=South Korea}} are serviced by {{ill|Asiana Airlines|en|Asiana Airlines|WD=Q211165|lt=Asiana Airlines|1=Asiana Airlines}} from {{ill|Matsuyama|en|Matsuyama|WD=Q200022|lt=Matsuyama|1=Matsuyama}} and {{ill|Takamatsu|en|Takamatsu|WD=Q200707|lt=Takamatsu|1=Takamatsu}}. There are periodic international charter flights as well.
